headline: Phylogenetic software gains mixture models, structure tests and concordance factors
label: Evolutionary Analysis Software Tools
summary: Updated IQ-TREE 3 and treestructure releases, plus a mixture-model simulation benchmark, address model choice and hidden population structure in phylogenetic…
synthesis: The three contributions share a thread of making richer evolutionary models usable within established phylogenetic workflows. IQ-TREE 3 consolidates mixture models, gene and site concordance factors, and divergence time integration into one open-source maximum-likelihood release. The accompanying simulation study supplies model-choice evidence for this functionality, reporting that across-site mixture models, particularly CAT-GTR, fit heterogeneous phylogenomic data best while maintaining accuracy on homogeneous data. The treestructure R package addresses a complementary problem by applying a coalescent-based statistical test to detect unobserved population structure in time-scaled phylogenetic trees. What is new is the integration of these capabilities into accessible tools rather than a new inference framework. The simulation study is evaluative rather than a software release, so the shared thread is dominant but not universal.
